The stdio path takes the raw JSON with no schema check, so if a server sends `"nextCursor": null` the loop keeps going (`null !== undefined`) and the next request goes out with `{ cursor: null }`. Depending on the server that either fails the whole listing or returns page one again and never stops. The SDK path doesn't hit this because its schema only accepts a string. Would narrowing it here be enough?

```suggestion
			cursor =
				typeof result.nextCursor === "string" ? result.nextCursor : undefined;
```

Also wondering if both loops should bail out when a server hands back the same cursor it was just sent, since right now that would spin until something else times out.
Fixed in 7d2aeef: stdio now accepts only string cursors, and both clients reject non-advancing cursors. Added three real-transport regressions; all 119 MCP tests pass.

In general, it is better if we can reflect the "only set for `beforeRun`" in a TypeScript shape which has `{foo: "beforeRun", entry: "run" | "continue", ...}` so the rest of the system can use these fields in a typesafe way. Also possible to lift a property out of an object by construction to relate these fields with some other state. (Does that make sense? TL;DR, can we use the type system here to communicate "only set for `beforeRun`" and benefit from checking?)

We probably almost always call this, so we could simplify the whole thing by always initializing `turnAccepted` in the constructor, make that type non-null and avoid some ?s, and avoid the conditional in `whenTurnAccepted`.

Stylistically, think `turnAccepted.then(...)` or `await turnAccepted` read better than `whenTurnAccepted().then(...)` or `await whenTurnAccepted`, so consider renaming `whenTurnAccepted`.

Half right, and the fix is the other half. The `null` is deliberate: an explicit `undefined` is swallowed by the parameter default, so the unlisted-model case would silently get the effort options instead of none. The bug was that my edit to widen the signature to `| null` did not apply, leaving the annotation saying `| undefined` while the body already normalised `null`. Signature corrected rather than the call site.

Fair catch. Before this PR a `metadata: null` clear was encoded as `{}` and the daemon wiped the record; my rewrite sent a literal `null`, which `asPlainRecord` decodes as omitted, so the clear became a no-op. No desktop or CLI caller passes `metadata: null` over the hub today, but it was a semantic change this diff introduced, so restored the `{}` encoding in 3e428e6dc and added a test for it.
